title: Spectral Fingerprints of Resonant Defect Scattering by Substitutional Mn in Graphene
authors: Ahmed Samir Lotfy, Zviadi Zarkua, Renan Villarreal, Rikkie Joris, Muhammad Saad, Koen van Stiphout, Karina Landivar, Steven Brems, Giovanni Di Santo, Aleksandr Seliverstov, Simona Achilli, Luca Petaccia, Lino M. C. Pereira
abstract: Using substitutional Mn in graphene/Cu(111) as a model point defect, we combine scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to test the predicted fingerprints of resonant scattering. As the Mn concentration increases to 0.44%, the Dirac point stretching reaches 0.52 eV, while momentum broadening remains energy independent. These spectral fingerprints classify substitutional Mn as a strong resonant scatterer and establish the combination of STM and ARPES as a powerful approach to identify and characterize resonant disorder in graphene.
summary: This work uses a combination of STM and ARPES on Mn-doped graphene to characterize disorder. By analyzing the spectral broadening of the Dirac cone, the authors distinguish the signature of strong resonant scattering from other types of disorder. The findings establish a quantitative method for measuring defect scattering strength in graphene, which is vital for controlling electronic properties in nanoscale devices.
main_problem: The paper aims to experimentally and theoretically test the spectral fingerprints associated with resonant defect scattering in graphene caused by substitutional Manganese (Mn) impurities.
main_result: The observed spectral broadening ($\Delta E_{	ext{DP}}$ and $\Delta k_L$) scales linearly with Mn concentration, providing strong evidence that Mn acts as a strong resonant scatterer in graphene.
method: The study combines Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements with Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) to characterize the defect concentration and spectral signatures.
model_or_system: The system is graphene/Cu(111) doped with substitutional Mn point defects. Theoretical modeling uses DFT to predict local electronic structure, while ARPES measures the quasiparticle spectral function $A(\mathbf{k}, \omega)$.
key_observables: Dirac point stretching ($\Delta E_{	ext{DP}}$), momentum broadening ($\Delta k_L$), and the effective scattering cross section ($\sigma_{eff}$).
important_parameters:
Mn concentration ($n_{	ext{Mn}}$), temperature (20 K, 78 K), and photon energy ($\hbar
u = 34 	ext{ eV}$).
main_assumptions: The linear increase of $\Delta k_L$ with $n_{	ext{Mn}}$ is assumed to be dominated by single-particle scattering from the substitutional defects.
figures_summary: Figures show STM images confirming Mn placement, DFT calculations predicting Mn-related spectral weight, and ARPES spectra comparing nonimplanted, low-concentration, and high-concentration samples, illustrating the progressive spectral changes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework distinguishing resonant vs. non-resonant scattering, then using STM to quantify the defect concentration, and finally applying ARPES to measure the correlated spectral changes ($\Delta E_{	ext{DP}}$ and $\Delta k_L$) that confirm the resonant scattering mechanism.
why_interesting: The quantitative link between a structurally identified defect (STM) and the resulting spectral broadening (ARPES) provides a powerful, measurable diagnostic tool for understanding disorder in 2D electron systems, which is crucial for designing quantum materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. STM and ARPES for (a) nonimplanted graphene/Cu(111), (b) nMn = 0.177 ± 0.013%, and (c) nMn = 0.44 ± 0.03%. (a1–c1) STM topographies (scale bar, 5 nm) acquired at (Itun, Vsample) = (0.10 nA, −0.30 V), (0.25 nA, 0.15 V), and (105.17 nA, 0.23 V), respectively. (a2– c2) ARPES spectra near K along Γ →K →M, obtained by summing separately acquired s- and p-polarization data. (a3– c3) Stacked momentum distribution curves (MDCs) from the s-polarization data used in the quantitative analysis. The red traces are individual MDCs at successive binding energies, and the blue symbols connected by a line mark the fitted MDC peak positions.

FIG. 3. Dirac point stretching. (a) kMDC(EB) after subtrac- tion of the fitted linear dispersion and normalization by the absolute sigmoidal amplitude (nMn is given in %; the symbols are extracted values and solid curves are the sigmoidal fits). (b) Stretching ∆EDP, defined as the 10–90% width of the fit- ted sigmoidal step, versus substitutional Mn concentration. Horizontal error bars in (b) denote the STM-derived concen- tration uncertainties; vertical error bars denote one standard deviation uncertainties propagated from the sigmoidal fits.

FIG. 2. Atomic structure and calculated electronic signa- ture of substitutional Mn in graphene/Cu(111). (a) Exper- imental constant-current STM image of an isolated defect (Itun = 0.48 nA, Vsample = 0.42 V; scale bar, 0.2 nm). (b) DFT-based constant-height STM simulation 3 ˚A above graphene. (c) Structural model, with Mn occupying a single carbon vacancy. (d) Density of states projected onto graphene (black) and Mn (red), referenced to EF. The Mn-derived peak and finite graphene spectral weight in the region of the Dirac point (around −0.3 eV) are consistent with hybridiza- tion; shading marks the relevant energy range.

FIG. 4. Momentum broadening. (a) Lorentzian MDC FWHM ∆kL versus binding energy for the three samples (nMn is given in %). (b) Energy-averaged ∆kL versus nMn; horizontal error bars denote the STM-derived uncertainty in nMn, and verti- cal error bars denote one standard deviation of ∆kL over the analyzed binding-energy range. The line is a linear fit whose slope gives the effective two-dimensional scattering cross sec- tion.
